name: TLV61046ADBVR
title: TLV61046A: 28 V boost converter with built-in rectifier diode and input-output isolation switch, SOT-23-6
summary: A small step-up converter that runs from 1.8 V to 5.5 V (and keeps running down to 1.6 V once started) and makes up to 28 V. The 30 V low-side switch, the rectifier diode and an isolation MOSFET between input and output are all inside, so the load is fully cut off from the supply when the part is disabled. It switches at a quasi-fixed 1.0 MHz in PWM and drops into pulse-frequency power save at light load. Tying FB to VIN gives a fixed 12 V with only an inductor and two capacitors; otherwise a divider on FB sets the output against a 0.795 V reference.

3.3 V to 28 V; 12 V fixed with FB tied to VIN

pins.name: SW
pins.function: Switching node, on the drain of the low-side power MOSFET inside. The inductor connects between VIN and this pin.

pins.name: FB
pins.function: Feedback input. With a resistor divider from VOUT, its tap sets the output voltage. Connected straight to VIN, it selects the internal feedback and the output regulates at 12 V.

pins.name: EN
pins.function: Enable. A logic high turns the converter on; a logic low shuts it down.

circuits.title: Simplified schematic
circuits.description: The basic adjustable boost. L1 runs from the input to SW; the diode and isolation switch are inside, so VOUT feeds C2 and the load directly. R1 from VOUT to FB over R2 to ground sets the output, shown as 4.5 V to 28 V, from a 1.8 V to 5.5 V input. C1 decouples the input; EN takes an on/off logic signal.

circuits.title: 12 V output boost converter (Figure 8-1)
circuits.description: 12 V at up to 50 mA from a 2.7 V to 4.2 V input. L1 10 µH runs from the input to SW. R1 1.0 MΩ from VOUT to FB over R2 71.5 kΩ to ground sets the output. C1 1.0 µF decouples the input and C2 4.7 µF sits on VOUT. EN takes an on/off logic signal.
notes: Design targets: 2.7 V to 4.2 V in, 12 V out, 50 mA, ±50 mV ripple.

circuits.title: Fixed 12 V output with FB tied to VIN (Figure 8-9)
circuits.description: The three-part version: FB joins VIN, which switches the part to its internal feedback and fixes the output at 12 V with no divider. L1 10 µH from the input to SW, C1 2.2 µF on the input, C2 10 µF on VOUT. Input 1.8 V to 5.5 V; EN takes an on/off logic signal.

equations.note: Assumes a ceramic capacitor with no ESR; with tantalum or aluminium electrolytics the ESR adds to the ripple.

operation.text: Current-mode boost with an adaptive constant off-time: from the ratio of input to output voltage the controller works out the off-time, so the frequency stays near 1.0 MHz. Inside are the low-side NMOS switch (30 V), a power diode as rectifier, and an isolation MOSFET able to cut the input off from the output. Loop compensation is internal and keeps the loop stable across broad spans of VIN, VOUT, inductor value and output capacitor value.

An ordinary boost conducts from input to output through inductor and diode even with the switch off, which causes start-up inrush, leakage into the load in shutdown and unlimited overload current. In the TLV61046A the isolation switch opens in shutdown and under overload, breaking that path, so the load is truly disconnected and shutdown leakage is minimal.
The converter stops when VIN falls below about 1.55 V and will not restart until VIN rises to about 1.75 V; the 200 mV hysteresis keeps it from misbehaving between those levels.

With VIN above the 1.8 V maximum UVLO rising threshold, a high on EN starts the part. A low on EN stops switching and opens the isolation switch, separating output from input; input current in shutdown is under 1 µA.

Start-up begins when EN goes high. First comes a pre-charge phase of about 2 ms in which the isolation FET turns on slowly and charges the output capacitor at about 30 mA. Switching then begins with the peak inductor current held to 140 mA while VOUT is under 3 V, rising gradually to the normal 980 mA as VOUT climbs from 3 V to 5 V. This switching phase lasts about 5 ms, for a total soft start of about 7 ms, and keeps inrush low.
Switching stops when VOUT passes the 29.2 V threshold and resumes once VOUT has dropped 0.9 V below it.
Below 4 V on VOUT the part limits output current, and the limit falls as VOUT falls; with VOUT shorted to ground the current is held under 200 mA.
The part shuts down when the junction passes about 150 °C and restarts when it has cooled to about 130 °C.

At moderate and heavy load the part runs quasi-fixed-frequency PWM near 1.0 MHz. Each cycle the NMOS switch turns on so current in the inductor rises while the output capacitor carries the load. When the current reaches the level set by the error amplifier (which compares FB with the internal reference), the switch turns off, the diode conducts and the inductor's energy goes to the output. The next cycle starts when the computed off-time ends.

As load falls the error amplifier lowers the peak current until it reaches a floor of 200 mA. Below that the output rises above its set point; when FB reaches the PFM reference (0.803 V typ against 0.795 V in PWM) the part enters power save. It switches a few more cycles, owing to comparator delay, then stops, and the output capacitor supplies the load until FB drops below the PFM reference, when switching resumes. In power save the output sits about 1 % above its PWM value.

Inductance 2.2 µH to 22 µH works; the key ratings are value, saturation current and DCR. Size it from the peak current equations. A ripple under 40 % of the average current is the usual aim at full load; a larger inductor lowers core loss and EMI but slows the transient response. Because the part is meant for low output currents, ripple up to 200 % of average with a small inductor is acceptable, which means it always works in DCM.

The output capacitor sets ripple and affects loop stability. Use 0.47 µF to 10 µF of effective capacitance; below that range the loop can go unstable, and more capacitance reduces PWM ripple. Ceramic capacitors lose capacitance with DC bias, ageing and AC signal, more than 50 % at rated voltage in some cases, so choose a voltage rating with margin. On the input, a ceramic of more than 1.0 µF suits most designs.

Supply between 1.8 V and 5.5 V, well regulated. If the source is several inches or more away, bulk capacitance beside the ceramic bypass may be needed, typically a 47 µF electrolytic or tantalum. The source must be rated for the current the converter draws at its input, output voltage and load.

The switching edges are very fast, so layout governs stability, noise and EMI. Keep every trace on SW short and small in area, and run a ground plane beneath the converter. Place the input capacitor close to both VIN and GND. The critical loop runs from the switch through the diode and output capacitor back to the switch's ground; keep it as short as possible, with the output capacitor close to both VOUT and GND to limit overshoot on SW and VOUT. In the example board a bottom-layer ground plane ties the top-side component grounds through vias.
